checks.invariant: limitar_subidas rejects /analyze bodies larger than MAX_UPLOAD_MB before they are received or stored
checks.result: upload_too_big (backend/app.py:180-186) reads only the Content-Length header, defaulting to '0' when it is absent and returning False on ValueError. A chunked request has no Content-Length and passes. FastAPI parses the whole multipart form, spooling the file part, before analyze runs, so the 200 MB counter at line 598 only limits the second copy into UPLOAD_DIR. Caddyfile sets no request_body limit, and port 8000 is also published. The same Content-Length-only pattern applies to /ingest (lines 627 and 632). Candidate backend/app.py:content-length-only-request-size-gates (needs_validation: Starlette/python-multipart versions, proxy forwarding, disk layout).

checks.invariant: Video analysis must not monopolise the shared server and must be bounded in frames/time
checks.result: analyze is declared async def (backend/app.py:577) and calls get_engine().analyze_video synchronously (line 603), with no asyncio.to_thread, unlike ws_live at line 569. It then calls insert_event (line 608) and dispatch_alerts (line 609; time.sleep(0.5) per event at line 351, plus a wait_for_publish of up to 5 s per command at actuator.py:59) on the event loop. analyze_video loops over every frame with no frame or duration cap (engine.py:69-78). backend/Dockerfile:25 starts a single uvicorn worker, and compose does not override it. Candidate backend/app.py:analyze:blocking-video-analysis-on-event-loop (proposed confirmed).

checks.invariant: Live inference capacity (engine.infer_lock and the asyncio default executor) is shared fairly; one principal cannot hold unbounded concurrent sessions or frame rate
checks.result: ws_live checks only session and camera ownership (resolve_camera, backend/cameras.py:149-162). It has no per-user or per-camera connection count and no frame rate or size check (backend/app.py:566-569). Each frame goes through asyncio.to_thread to the default executor, which is shared with /ingest (line 623) and the limitar_subidas session lookup (line 476), and then waits on the single process-wide infer_lock (engine.py:48, 133). The only pacing is in the browser (backend/templates/index.html:761-772). Candidate backend/app.py:ws_live:unbounded-concurrent-inference-sessions (needs_validation). The process-global per-level alert cooldown in dispatch_live_alert (backend/app.py:359-372) belongs to the alert-dispatch unit (h4-mqtt-alerts) and is not assessed here.

checks.invariant: Temporary upload files are removed on every path and do not accumulate
checks.result: Covered. tempfile.mkstemp creates a unique file in UPLOAD_DIR (line 589). The finally block at lines 611-615 removes it after the 413 early return, analysis exceptions and success. Startup clean_leftovers (lines 167-177) removes vigia_upload_* files left by a crash. Client disconnect before the handler leaves no UPLOAD_DIR file. The Starlette spool is a separate concern, covered by the Content-Length check above.

checks.result: analyze_video calls self.detector.detect and self.pose.analyze (engine.py:78-82) without infer_lock. Live sessions take the lock from worker threads (engine.py:133). checks.result: Covered. clean_filename (backend/app.py:75-80) normalises backslashes and takes the basename. It maps every character outside [A-Za-z0-9._-] to '_', collapses runs of dots, strips leading and trailing '._-' and keeps the last 80 characters. The label is used only as the mkstemp suffix (the lowercased extension, line 589) and inside evt_{label}_{stamp}.jpg (engine.py:88), so no separator or traversal can reach either path.

checks.result: Covered. mkstemp (exclusive create, 0600, random name) is used in UPLOAD_DIR. The file is removed in finally on every return or exception path (lines 611-615) and swept at startup. No predictable temp name and no TOCTOU between creation and use.

checks.invariant: Evidence objects are unique per owner, so one user's analysis cannot overwrite or inherit another user's evidence
checks.result: Fails. The evidence name is evt_{sanitised client filename}_{int(video_time*1000):08d}.jpg (engine.py:87-88), with no user, community or random component. cv2.imwrite writes it into the single shared EVIDENCE_DIR (engine.py:95; backend/app.py:30). insert_event uses a global UNIQUE storage_key with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING (backend/app.py:248; schema line 186). A same-name collision therefore lets the later writer replace the file while losing its own row, and the earlier row owner is served the later user's frame (backend/app.py:669-683). Candidate engine.py:analyze_video:evidence-filename-not-owner-unique (needs_validation: deliberate collision depends on model detections at chosen frames).

checks.result: Only the extension is checked (backend/app.py:586-588). No exfiltration channel is source-visible: only frames with a detected person are stored, and only for the uploader. Recorded as hardening, not a candidate.

Notifier.send_photo opens it (notifier.py:42-67), and no traversal is possible. The file read can be another user's frame if a same-name collision overwrote it, which is the same root cause as the evidence-collision candidate. The Telegram channel scope belongs to h4-mqtt-alerts.

checks.result: Covered. manage.py issues secrets.token_urlsafe(32) and stores only its SHA-256 (backend/manage.py:96-101). edge_from_token matches token_hash with status = 'active' on every request, with no cache (backend/auth.py:214-223). candidates.title: Edge device can claim arbitrary evidence filenames in the shared events directory for its community
candidates.description: POST /ingest accepts an attacker-chosen 'image' filename from an edge device. It inserts that name as media_files.storage_key for the device's community without checking that the device produced, uploaded or owns the file. storage_key is a single global UNIQUE namespace over the one shared EVIDENCE_DIR, and insert_event uses ON CONFLICT (storage_key) DO NOTHING, so the first claimant owns a name. /evidence authorises a community_admin from that row (a NULL camera passes the admin filter) and then serves whatever file currently exists under the name. An edge token of community A can therefore pre-claim a predictable evidence name that a resident of community B will later produce through /analyze (evt_{sanitised upload filename}_{8-digit millisecond offset}.jpg). When B's analysis writes the file, B's media row is silently not inserted, so B and B's admin lose access to the image, and community A's admin can fetch B's private evidence frame through /evidence. A's dashboard also shows the frame as the image of A's injected event. Any file in events/ without a media_files row can be claimed the same way after the fact. This extension depends on deployment and is not part of the confirmed claim: when the optional compose profile 'live' runs main.py on the same ./events volume, its unowned files (fixed-name events.jsonl, intruso_YYYYmmdd_HHMMSS.jpg, clip_YYYYmmdd_HHMMSS.mp4) are also claimable. live_ evidence names use microsecond timestamps and are not practically predictable.
candidates.root_cause: insert_event trusts a client-chosen object key, validated only for its character set by IMAGE_NAME_RE, as a storage_key in a tenant-agnostic global namespace with first-writer-wins conflict handling. /evidence binds authorisation to that row, not to the principal that produced the file on disk.
candidates.intended_behavior: An edge device should only be able to attach evidence objects that it uploaded, under a server-generated key in a namespace bound to its own device and community. A storage-key conflict must never silently drop or transfer ownership of another principal's evidence.

A community_admin account in community A to read the claimed name through /evidence (or a resident owning an edge-assigned private camera if camera_id is supplied).

execution.attacker_perspective: Community A's edge device and community A's administrator targeting evidence produced by a resident of community B.
payloads: POST /ingest with Authorization: Bearer <edge token of community A> and body {"level":"BAJO","score":0,"people":0,"image":"evt_video.mp4_00000300.jpg"}
GET /evidence/evt_video.mp4_00000300.jpg as community A's admin, after a community B resident analyses a file named video.mp4 whose event fires at 0.3 s
instructions: Source review only. No target code, database or service was executed in this run because no OS-enforced sandbox was available.
Followed the edge payload through validate_event (character-set check), insert_event (global storage_key with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING), and the /evidence admin query and FileResponse.
Followed a victim /analyze through analyze_video naming and cv2.imwrite into the same directory, and through insert_event reaching the same conflict clause.
execution.observed_result: Source shows that the edge row is inserted under community A with camera NULL, and that the victim's later media insert for the same name does nothing. It also shows that the /evidence admin query for community A returns the edge row and the handler serves the file on disk, which is the victim's image. This was not observed at runtime.

Generate evidence keys on the server (for example uuid4 hex) and scope them per community: UNIQUE(community_id, storage_key) plus a per-community subdirectory. For /ingest, accept the image bytes, or a reference to an object the same device uploaded, and reject unknown names. Treat a storage_key conflict as an error instead of DO NOTHING.

likelihood.reason: The attack needs an operator-provisioned device token and an admin account in the same community. It also needs prior knowledge of a victim's upload filename and frame timing, or the name of an unowned file.

impact.reason: Another community's private-camera evidence image is disclosed to community A's admin, and the victim silently loses their own evidence record.

candidates.title: /analyze evidence filenames can collide across users, so one tenant can overwrite or inherit another tenant's evidence image
candidates.description: analyze_video names each evidence frame evt_{label}_{stamp}.jpg, where label is the sanitised client filename and stamp is the event's millisecond offset in the video. The name has no user, community or random component, and cv2.imwrite writes it into the single shared EVIDENCE_DIR, overwriting any existing file. insert_event then inserts the media_files row with ON CONFLICT (storage_key) DO NOTHING. Two users in any communities can upload files with the same sanitised name whose events fire at the same sampled frame and fps. In that case the later upload overwrites the earlier owner's image on disk and loses its own row. The earlier owner, and that owner's community admin when admin_can_view is set, then receive the later user's private frame from /evidence, while the later user's event shows no image. An attacker who first uploads videos under a guessed victim filename, with events at the victim's frame offsets, captures the victim's frames. Uploading after a victim instead replaces the victim's stored evidence with attacker content.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: Evidence object names derive only from the client-controlled filename and video-relative time, not from a server-generated unique or owner-scoped key. The shared directory and the global first-writer-wins storage_key let a later writer's file replace an object owned by an earlier principal.

video_time = idx / fps is fully determined by frame index and container fps.
The stamp is the zero-padded millisecond offset; there is no unique or owner component.
storage_key is UNIQUE globally across communities.
One EVIDENCE_DIR is shared by all users and communities.
list_events picks the image by event_id, so the later user's event has no image after the conflict.

blockers: Causing a collision on purpose needs attacker-supplied video content that makes the YOLO pipeline emit a MEDIO/ALTO event at the same sampled frame index and fps as the victim's event. That depends on model inference, which was not executed: this run had no OS-enforced sandbox, models or database.
The attacker must know or guess the victim's sanitised upload filename, and how predictable real client filenames are in the deployed user base cannot be determined from source.

validation_plan.local: Use a sandbox with a disposable PostgreSQL loaded from bd_intivision/schema_vigia.sql, two dummy communities with residents X and Y, and PersonDetector.detect stubbed to return three person boxes on every frame (or the real models). Prepare two small, visually distinct 30 fps MP4 fixtures, both named clip.mp4. POST /analyze as X, then as Y. Expect events/evt_clip.mp4_<stamp>.jpg to hold Y's frame, no media_files row for Y's events, and GET /evidence/evt_clip.mp4_<stamp>.jpg as X to return Y's frame. Stop at the first matching file.

candidates.title: /analyze runs whole-video YOLO analysis synchronously on the only event loop, stalling the service for every tenant
candidates.description: The analyze endpoint is declared async def but calls get_engine().analyze_video(...) directly, followed by insert_event and dispatch_alerts, all of which are synchronous. analyze_video decodes every frame and runs YOLO (plus pose when a person is detected) on every third frame, with no frame, duration or time cap. dispatch_alerts sleeps 0.5 s per event and can wait up to 5 s per MQTT publish and 10 s per Telegram request. The shipped backend image runs a single uvicorn worker. While one resident's upload is analysed, that event loop cannot accept or advance any other HTTP request, WebSocket frame, /ingest call or login from any user or community, and a client disconnect cannot cancel the work. Analysis time grows with the frame count of an upload of up to 200 MB, and the uploader controls frame count, resolution and the number of events.
candidates.root_cause: CPU-bound and network-bound blocking work runs inline in an async FastAPI handler instead of in a bounded worker thread or process with a concurrency limit and a frame/time budget.
candidates.intended_behavior: Video analysis should run off the event loop in a bounded queue (for example one or a few concurrent analyses, with per-user limits). It should have a maximum frame count or duration and stop when the client disconnects, and it must not delay other users' requests or live streams.

trace.description: async def handler, which runs on the event loop thread.
get_engine().analyze_video(...) is called synchronously, with no asyncio.to_thread or executor.
while True: cap.read() runs over every frame with no frame or time cap.
YOLO inference for every sampled frame runs on the event loop thread, blocking all other requests until analysis ends.

evidence.description: ws_live offloads per-frame work with asyncio.to_thread, a control that /analyze does not have.
A synchronous DB insert per event runs on the event loop.
time.sleep(0.5) per event runs on the event loop inside dispatch_alerts.
wait_for_publish(timeout=5) runs for each siren or LED command sent from dispatch_alerts.
uvicorn is started without --workers, giving a single process and event loop; docker-compose.yml does not override it.
MAX_UPLOAD_MB caps bytes only; there is no frame or duration cap anywhere on the path.
Inference runs on every sample_every-th decoded frame (3 in config.yaml).

The backend runs the shipped single-worker uvicorn command. With N workers, N concurrent uploads stall all of them.
The uploader has an active private camera, or one is auto-created by default_camera.

Confirmed that analyze is async def and calls analyze_video, insert_event and dispatch_alerts without asyncio.to_thread or run_in_executor.
Confirmed that analyze_video iterates every decoded frame with no frame or time limit and calls YOLO synchronously.
Confirmed that backend/Dockerfile starts a single uvicorn worker and that docker-compose.yml does not override the command.

candidates.title: One user can open unlimited /ws/live sessions and starve other tenants' live detection on the shared inference lock and thread pool
candidates.description: /ws/live accepts any number of concurrent connections per user and per camera. Each connection processes as many frames as its client sends; the only pacing is the dashboard's client-side JavaScript. Each frame is decoded and run through YOLO and pose in asyncio's default thread pool, serialised on the single process-wide engine.infer_lock. A resident can open many connections and stream small valid JPEG frames back-to-back. That keeps every default-executor thread occupied while blocked on infer_lock and wins most acquisitions of the non-FIFO lock. Other residents' live sessions, in any community, then get a fraction of inference throughput, and other asyncio.to_thread work queues behind it: /ingest token lookups and inserts, WebSocket authentication and the /analyze session check. This degrades the live-detection safety function for unrelated users for as long as the connections stay open.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: The server has no per-user or per-camera limit on concurrent live sessions or frame rate and no fair scheduling for the shared inference lock. The design relies on the browser client pacing itself.

trace.description: Authenticated WebSocket with no limit on concurrent connections per user or camera.
resolve_camera checks ownership only; it does not count sessions.
receive_bytes loop with no rate, count or application size limit.
Each frame is submitted with asyncio.to_thread to the shared default executor.
cv2.imdecode runs on attacker bytes outside the lock.
with eng.infer_lock: detect and pose run under one process-wide lock shared by all tenants.

evidence.description: A single threading.Lock is shared by all clients (non-FIFO).
The only pacing is client-side (one frame in flight); the comment says the model never saturates, but the server does not enforce it.
resolve_camera matches an own, active, private camera and keeps no connection accounting.
/ingest token lookup uses asyncio.to_thread and shares the default executor.
The limitar_subidas session lookup uses asyncio.to_thread and shares the default executor.
A single process hosts every tenant's live sessions.

blockers: The default executor size, min(32, CPU count + 4), and per-inference latency depend on the deployed host's CPU count and torch threading, which source does not show.
How much starvation occurs depends on threading.Lock acquisition order under contention and on frame decode cost at runtime. Nothing could be executed in this run.
Whether an upstream layer (Caddy, host firewall) limits concurrent WebSocket connections per client is a deployment fact. The repository Caddyfile sets no such limit.

validation_plan.local: In a sandbox with CPU and memory limits, set up a disposable database, two dummy residents in two communities, and either the real detector or a fixed-latency stub (for example sleep 50 ms under infer_lock). Open one victim connection that sends one small JPEG per response, and N = 4, 8 and 16 attacker connections that send 1 KB JPEGs back-to-back. Record the victim's frames per second and the latency of a concurrent /ingest request made with a dummy edge token. Stop once victim throughput clearly falls as about 1/(N+1).
validation_plan.deployment: The owner checks the host CPU count, whether any proxy or firewall limits concurrent WebSockets per client IP or user, and the expected number of simultaneous live users.

candidates.title: Upload and ingest size limits rely only on the declared Content-Length, so chunked bodies are fully buffered before any limit applies
candidates.description: limitar_subidas is meant to reject /analyze uploads larger than MAX_UPLOAD_MB before they are received, but upload_too_big only reads the Content-Length header, and a missing header defaults to '0'. A request sent with Transfer-Encoding: chunked carries no Content-Length and passes. FastAPI and Starlette then parse the entire multipart body and spool the file part to a temporary file before the analyze handler runs. The handler's 200 MB counter only limits the second copy into UPLOAD_DIR. The repository Caddyfile sets no request body limit, and port 8000 is also published. An authenticated resident can therefore stream an arbitrarily large body into the container's temporary storage on the shared host disk for as long as the request lasts. /ingest has the same pattern: its 100 kB check reads only Content-Length, and request.json() buffers the whole chunked body in memory for any edge-device token holder.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: Body size is enforced from a client-declared header instead of counting bytes actually read during parsing; neither the ASGI layer nor the proxy applies a streaming limit.

trace.description: Middleware for POST /analyze: session check, then size check.
upload_too_big(request) is the only pre-receipt size control.
int(request.headers.get('content-length', '0')): a chunked request is treated as 0 bytes.
call_next passes the request on; FastAPI parses the full multipart form before invoking the handler.
The UploadFile parameter is already spooled in full to a temporary file by the framework, with no size limit, before this handler runs.

evidence.description: The docstring states the intent to reject huge uploads before receiving them, using Content-Length.
The handler's byte counter applies only while copying out of the already-parsed UploadFile.
/ingest checks size through Content-Length only.
request.json() reads the entire body into memory.
reverse_proxy has no request_body max_size.
The backend port 8000 is published directly, bypassing the proxy.
fastapi>=0.110.0 is unpinned, so the installed Starlette/python-multipart spooling behaviour depends on the build.

blockers: The Starlette and python-multipart versions installed in the image are unpinned. For the built image, confirm whether multipart file parts have any size limit and where they are spooled.
Whether Caddy, and any host or CDN in front of it, forwards chunked request bodies to the backend without a bound is a deployment fact.
The container's temporary-directory location, its disk capacity, and whether that disk is shared with ./events and PostgreSQL are deployment facts.

validation_plan.local: In a sandbox with TMPDIR on a small size-limited tmpfs (for example 64 MB) and MAX_UPLOAD_MB=1, run the backend with a dummy session. POST /analyze with Transfer-Encoding: chunked and a 5 MB multipart file part, and observe that limitar_subidas does not return 413 and that the spool file in TMPDIR grows past 1 MB before the handler's own 413. Repeat for /ingest with a dummy edge token and a 1 MB chunked JSON body, measuring process RSS growth. Stop at the first exceedance.
validation_plan.deployment: The owner confirms Caddy request_body limits (none are set in the Caddyfile), whether port 8000 is reachable from the Internet, and the free space of the filesystem backing the container's /tmp.

candidates.title: Evidence images are written to shared disk without per-user quota or retention, so one resident can exhaust storage for all communities
candidates.description: Every MEDIO/ALTO event writes a full-resolution JPEG of the decoded frame into the shared events/ directory, which is bind-mounted as host ./events. /analyze produces one per 5 s of video time with no frame or duration cap, and /ws/live one per 5 s per session with unlimited sessions. No code deletes evidence files, caps per-user totals, or enforces the per-user quota the schema defines (plans.storage_gb and v_user_storage.quota_bytes). File size follows the decoded frame resolution, which the uploader controls. A compact video of a static high-resolution scene containing a person can therefore turn one upload of at most 200 MB into many large evidence files. When the shared disk fills, other tenants' evidence writes fail silently (cv2.imwrite returns False and the event is still recorded), as can anything else on the same filesystem.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: Persisted evidence is not accounted per principal and has no quota, size cap or retention, and the write paths never enforce the schema-level quota (plans.storage_gb / v_user_storage).

trace.description: An authenticated resident uploads a video (or streams through /ws/live, engine.py:153).
One event per 5 s of video time, for the whole video, with no frame cap.
cv2.imwrite writes a full-resolution JPEG of the frame into the shared directory permanently.

evidence.description: Live sessions persist one evidence image per event per session.
Live sessions write into the shared EVIDENCE_DIR.
plans.storage_gb defines a per-plan storage quota.
The v_user_storage quota view exists but is never referenced by application code.
The evidence directory is a host bind mount shared by all tenants.
MAX_UPLOAD_MB caps input bytes only, not decoded output volume.

blockers: How many bytes each event can write (the decoded-resolution limits of the bundled FFmpeg/OpenCV, and the JPEG size of attacker-chosen frames) can only be learned by running the decoder, which was not done.
The host's disk capacity, whether ./events shares a filesystem with PostgreSQL data and Docker storage, and any operator cleanup job are deployment facts.

validation_plan.local: In a sandbox with a 256 MB disk quota on the events directory and a stub detector that forces ALTO on every sampled frame, upload one small (at most 5 MB) synthetic MP4 of a static high-resolution scene as a dummy resident. Measure total bytes written to events/ against the input size, and stop at the quota.
validation_plan.deployment: The owner checks the disk capacity and filesystem layout of ./events, whether PostgreSQL shares that filesystem, and whether any retention or cleanup runs.

hardening: IMAGE_NAME_RE (backend/app.py) accepts '.' and '..'. An edge device can store storage_key '..', so /evidence joins EVIDENCE_DIR with '..' and calls FileResponse on a directory: a server error, but no file disclosure. Reject dot-only names in validate_event and /evidence.

engine.py analyze_video calls the shared YOLO detector and pose models without engine.infer_lock, while live sessions call them under the lock from other threads. Concurrent predict on one ultralytics model is not documented as thread-safe and may produce wrong detections or exceptions. No cross-principal effect was established.

/analyze accepts any bytes whose filename has a video extension, and cv2.VideoCapture lets the FFmpeg bundled in opencv-python-headless pick a demuxer by probing the content. Consider limiting demuxers and protocols (for example OPENCV_FFMPEG_CAPTURE_OPTIONS with protocol_whitelist;file) or checking container signatures. No exfiltration channel was found: only person-detected frames are stored, and they go back only to the uploader.

uncovered.surface: WS /ws/live frame decoding and /analyze frame decoding
uncovered.boundary: Decoded image dimension and memory limits (cv2.imdecode, cv2.VideoCapture)
uncovered.subsystem: Media decoding in backend/app.py and engine.py
uncovered.reason: _process_frame calls cv2.imdecode on attacker bytes before any pixel or dimension check (backend/app.py:528). Messages can be up to the server's WebSocket limit, with no application cap, and decoding runs in parallel threads outside infer_lock. A small, highly compressible JPEG or video can declare very large dimensions, and frame.copy and imwrite allocate again. No unit selected the computational-amplification classes, so memory amplification from frame decoding has no owner.

uncovered.surface: Pre-authentication POST /login and POST /ingest database access
uncovered.reason: ThreadedConnectionPool (DB_POOL_MAX default 10, backend/db.py:24-25) raises PoolError at once when exhausted, which is mapped to a 503 for every route. auth.authenticate holds a pooled connection while running bcrypt, including the dummy hash for unknown users (backend/auth.py:95-123). edge_from_token runs a DB UPDATE for any bearer value before any size or rate gate. Concurrent unauthenticated attempts could therefore deny database access to all tenants. No unit owns the shared pool.

uncovered.boundary: Request body size before authentication; no app-level or Caddy body limit
uncovered.reason: limitar_subidas applies only to /analyze. FastAPI parses Form bodies, urlencoded or multipart (with file parts spooled to disk), before the handler and before current_user, and POST /login is unauthenticated. The Caddyfile sets no request_body limit, and how big a body is accepted depends on the Starlette version. This lies outside the /analyze boundary assigned here.
